import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

    call = API::moduleImport("urllib").getMember("request").getMember("urlretrieve").getACall() or

    call = API::moduleImport("pathlib").getMember("Path").getMember("read_bytes").getACall()

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Identify Resource Access in Library Code
 * @description Find calls to open() and urllib in the library source code (excluding tests) to identify potential SSRF or LFI sinks.
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/resource-access-audit
 * @tags security
 *       audit
 */

import python
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call, File f
where
  call.getLocation().getFile() = f and
  not f.getRelativePath().matches("%noxfile%") and
  not f.getRelativePath().matches("suite/%") and
  (
    call = API::builtin("open").getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("urllib.request").getMember("urlopen").getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("requests").getMember(["get", "post", "put", "delete", "request"]).getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("httpx").getMember(["get", "post", "put", "delete", "request"]).getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("aiohttp").getMember("ClientSession").getMember(["get", "post"]).getACall()
  )
select call, "Resource access detected in library code."
findings.hypothesis: The library may perform file or network I/O, which could be a vector for SSRF or LFI if user input controls the target.
